summary: Siuslaw NF lookout site 7 miles south of Florence, OR: 20-ft L-4 pole tower built 1932-33, forest guard A. G. Hines in 1933, removed 1959; registered as a former site in 2011.

facts.design: 20-ft round fir pole tower with L-4 cab
facts.status_note: Removed in 1959 per FFLOS and the Oregon Lookouts timeline; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1959.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Siuslaw National Forest

events.note: July 1, 1932 Siuslaw Oar: Forest Service crew have the road about completed to the top; lumber due for the new station
Oregon Lookouts timeline: 20-ft round fir pole tower with L-4 cab constructed; Siuslaw Oar, July 1932: lumber due for the new station. Register and firelookout.com give 1933.

Forest guard A. G. Hines moved his family to the new Siltcoos guard station (undated Siuslaw Oar item between August 19 and October 7, 1932; story reads it as late summer 1932); station closed for the season by late October 1932 (Siuslaw Oar, October 28, 1932)
Register and firelookout.com both date construction to 1933
A. G. Hines took up his duties as forest guard at the Siltcoos lookout station (April 1933)
Newly installed fire finder reported to have spotted a fire on Bailey hill near Junction City (Siuslaw Oar, July 1933)
Road to the lookout station widened to 18 feet by J.H. Newman and crew
Bill Brown appointed to take charge of the Siltcoos recreation area and to be stationed at the lookout after Labor Day (Eugene Guard, August 1941)
Timeline entry: activated March 10, 1942, Eugene Filter Center; no further detail given
Tower removed in 1959 (FFLOS; Oregon Lookouts timeline). firelookout.com says destroyed in 1959.
Registered March 29, 2011 as FFLOS US 905, OR 272; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Oregon Lookouts timeline and the 1932 newspaper items point to 1932; the Register and firelookout.com say 1933. The story reports both.
The Register says half a mile; firelookout.com says a mile.
The Register and the Oregon Lookouts timeline say removed in 1959; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1959. The year agrees.

notes_for_editor: No source read describes what remains at the site today or whether it is open to the public. A search returned an FFLA social media post saying the lookout was about one mile from the coast (search snippet only, not read or cited). The 1932/1933 construction-year conflict is the main open question. The 1941 recreation area reference is historical only.
